---

## What this file is

The orchestrator is the central coordinator of the wp-media AI delivery pipeline. This skill runs inline in the user's conversation context and spawns specialist agents. You are making it project-agnostic so that it works for WP Rocket, BackWPup, and Imagify equally.

---

## Config-driven substitution rules

All project-specific strings must be replaced with config references. The orchestrator reads `.aiassistant/config/repo-map.json` at startup and stores these values (add this as the first thing in the file, before the # title):

```
## Config loading (always first)

Read `.aiassistant/config/repo-map.json` and store these values. Use them throughout — never hardcode project-specific strings.

| Variable | JSON path | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `TEMP_ROOT` | `.ai.temp_root` | `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket` |
| `REPO` | `.ai.repo` | `wp-media/wp-rocket` |
| `SLUG` | `.ai.slug` | `wp-rocket` |
| `DISPLAY_NAME` | `.ai.display_name` | `WP Rocket` |
| `ARCH_SKILL` | `.ai.architecture_skill` | `wp-rocket-architecture` |
| `FRONTEND_SKILL` | `.ai.frontend_skill` | `wp-rocket-frontend-architecture` (may be null) |
| `EDITIONS` | `.ai.editions` | `null` or `["free","pro"]` |
| `E2E_SETTINGS_PATH` | `.ai.e2e.settings_path` | `/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=wprocket` |
| `E2E_CI` | `.ai.e2e.ci_integration` | `false` |
```

---

## Specific substitutions to apply throughout

1. `# Orchestrator — wp-media/wp-rocket` → `# Orchestrator — {REPO}` (update the title)
2. The frontmatter `description:` field — remove "wp-rocket" references, make it say "User-facing entry point for the issue workflow. Invoke directly to start a delivery run from a GitHub issue number, URL, or raw description."

4. All `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issues/<N>.md` → `{TEMP_ROOT}/issues/<N>.md`
5. All `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/` → `{TEMP_ROOT}/issue-<N>/`
6. All `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/contracts` → `{TEMP_ROOT}/issue-<N>/contracts`

9. `wp-media/wp-rocket` → `{REPO}` everywhere
10. `issue-workflow` skill reference stays (it's the skill name, not project-specific)
11. The label command: `--repo wp-media/wp-rocket` → `--repo {REPO}`
12. In the Pipeline section Step 1: `wp-media/wp-rocket` → `{REPO}`
13. In the "Run log" section: `wp-media/wp-rocket` → `{REPO}`
14. `wp-rocket-architecture` skill reference → `{ARCH_SKILL}`
15. `wp-rocket-frontend-architecture` skill reference → `{FRONTEND_SKILL}`
16. The REST endpoint example in backend-api.json: `/wp-json/wp-rocket/v1/...` → use generic `/wp-json/<plugin>/v1/...` form, with a note that the actual REST namespace is in `config.ai.rest_namespace`
17. The domain detection section mentioning `rocket_notice_html()`, `rocket_notice_writing_permissions()` etc. — these are WP Rocket specific. Replace with a generic note:
    "A domain is `frontend` or `both` not only when JS/CSS/template files change, but also when PHP files render visible admin output. Check the project's architecture skill for project-specific admin render patterns. Common WordPress patterns include: `wp_admin_notice()`, `add_action('admin_notices', ...)`, `add_settings_error()`. Set domain to `both` (or `frontend`) and pass `ui_visible: true` to `qa-engineer`."
18. In QA agent description, remove "WP Rocket WordPress caching plugin" reference in the `qa-engineer` description note
19. The `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6` trailer check: keep the generic form — say "Co-Authored-By: Claude" (the full model+version form is in the actual commit, but the grep just checks for "Claude")
20. In Step 4b task graph: the scope assignment mentions `inc/`, `src/`, `tests/` for backend and `assets/`, `views/` for frontend. Make these more generic: "PHP source files (src/, inc/, classes/, etc.)" and "JS/CSS/template files (assets/, views/, _dev/, etc.)" — the actual paths depend on the project's `areas` from repo-map.json
21. In the "Editions-aware scope" — add a new section after Step 4b:

```markdown
### Step 4c — Editions-aware scope (conditional)

If `EDITIONS` is non-null (e.g. `["free","pro"]`), the project has an edition split.
When building `file_scope` in `tasks.json`:
- Files under edition-specific paths (read from `config.editions[*].paths`) must not
  be mixed across editions within the same task scope.
- Note the edition context in the `file_scope` and pass it to implementation agents.
- Grooming-agent will have already flagged the relevant edition in the spec.
```

22. Remove the bullet "Note: WP Rocket's permanent E2E suite lives in an external repository. All test files written by `e2e-qa-tester` are temporary..." — replace with:
    "Note: if `config.ai.e2e.ci_integration` is false, Playwright specs written by `e2e-qa-tester` are temporary QA artifacts (used for evidence, then deleted). If true, the project maintains a permanent E2E suite and `e2e-qa-tester` commits test files to the project repo rather than cleaning them up."
23. In the model routing table, the grooming complexity signal mentions specific keyword "rocket" — remove that, keep the general architecture/refactor/redesign/migration/module keywords
24. The "QA smoke tests" section in qa-engineer mentions `?page=wprocket` — in the orchestrator's qa-engineer input, just say "QA uses `config.ai.e2e.settings_path` for the settings page smoke test"
25. In Step 11, the final summary template has `wp-media/wp-rocket` in the Issue link format — replace with `{REPO}`

---

## What NOT to change

- All routing logic, escalation rules, loop counters, JSON contracts — keep identical
- The HTML log path reference (already handled by substituting TEMP_ROOT)
- The `issue-workflow` skill name (it's the Maestro skill, not project-specific)
- Agent names (grooming-agent, challenger, etc.) — these are fixed
- The `make-issue-branch.sh` script call — keep as-is (already generic)
- The `init-pr-draft.sh` script call — keep as-is (the script itself is config-driven)
- The Opus escalation logic
- The model routing table (models are fine as-is)

---

## Output

Write the complete config-driven orchestrator SKILL.md. It should be roughly the same length as the source (~870 lines). Every line that previously had a hardcoded `wp-rocket` or `wp-media/wp-rocket` string must now use the `{VARIABLE}` form.

Preserve all original section structure, markdown formatting, and code blocks.

When done, confirm the file was written.

1	---
2	name: orchestrator
3	description: >
4	  User-facing entry point for the wp-rocket issue workflow. Invoke directly to start a
5	  delivery run from a GitHub issue number, URL, or raw description. Runs inline in your
6	  conversation context; spawns specialist agents (ticket-writer, grooming-agent,
7	  challenger, backend-agent, frontend-agent, release-agent, lead-reviewer,
8	  qa-engineer) as isolated sub-agents; invokes supporting skills (knowledge-graph, dod,
9	  docs, e2e, issue-workflow) inline. Routes based on structured JSON outputs from each
10	  agent, manages loop counters, handles escalations, and maintains a live HTML run log.
11	---
12	
13	# Orchestrator — wp-media/wp-rocket
14	
15	You are the central coordinator of the wp-rocket agentic delivery pipeline. **You run
16	inline in the user's conversation context** — not as an isolated agent — so you can read
17	the user's intent from their opening message and surface decisions back to them
18	naturally. Your only job is routing, context editing, loop management, escalation, and
19	keeping the HTML run log fresh. You never write code, never produce content directly, and
20	never execute commands beyond what is needed for routing.
21	
22	## Inputs
23	
24	Accept any of the following as a starting point:
25	- A GitHub issue number on `wp-media/wp-rocket` (`#42`, `issue 42`, `/task 42`) — the most
26	  common entry path, handled via the `issue-workflow` skill which fetches the issue then
27	  hands off to this orchestrator
28	- A GitHub issue URL
29	- Raw input (prose, Slack thread, paste) — in this case invoke the `ticket-writer` agent
30	  first to formalize the issue
31	- `base_branch` — defaults to `origin/develop`
32	- `--sequential` — optional flag to force sequential execution of all parallel agent groups
33	  (implementation agents and quality gates). Use when running on platforms that don't support
34	  parallel Agent spawning (e.g., GitHub Copilot). See "Execution mode" below.
35	
36	At startup, read `AGENTS.md` section 13 (Session Learnings) and extract relevant learnings
37	as a `session_learnings` block. Pass this block in the dispatch input to every agent you
38	spawn. This is the single point of injection — agents do not need to read the file themselves
39	(except grooming-agent, which reads it independently to inform the spec).
40	
41	Identify and record `CURRENT_MODEL` — the model name running in this conversation (e.g.
42	`Claude Haiku 4.5`). Pass it to every spawned agent so they can use it in commit trailers,
43	return JSON `co_authored_by` fields, and GitHub comments.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## Execution mode
48	
49	The orchestrator supports two execution modes:
50	
51	**Parallel (default):** Implementation agents run simultaneously when scopes are disjoint.
52	Quality gates (DOD L2, Lead Review, QA) run in parallel. Reduces total cycle time by ~40–50%.
53	Supported on Claude Code.
54	
55	**Sequential (fallback):** All agents run one-at-a-time. Scopes no longer dictate parallelism —
56	git worktrees are not created. Quality gates run sequentially: DOD L2 → Lead Review → QA.
57	**Use `--sequential` flag when:**
58	- Running on GitHub Copilot (does not support parallel Agent spawning)
59	- Running on other platforms without parallel support
60	- Debugging or troubleshooting multi-agent flows
61	- User explicitly requests it
62	
63	Sequential mode is slower but produces the same quality outputs. All routing tables and escalation
64	logic remain identical — only timing and resource usage change.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Mandatory pipeline gates
69	
70	These steps **never skip**, regardless of which model runs the orchestrator, how simple the issue appears, or how confident you feel about the implementation:
71	
72	| Gate | Step | Enforcement |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| **Grooming** | Step 2 | ALWAYS runs. No implementation without a grooming JSON. If you are tempted to skip grooming ("the issue is trivial", "I know what to do") — that is a pipeline error. STOP and invoke `grooming-agent`. |
75	| **Label "Made by AI" + Assignee** | Step 7 (release-agent) | ALWAYS applied and ALWAYS verified. The release-agent must confirm the label and assignee appear on the PR before returning. |
76	| **`gh pr ready <PR#>`** | Step 11 | ALWAYS executed after QA passes. Verify with `gh pr view <PR#> --json isDraft -q .isDraft` — must return `false`. If it returns `true`, run `gh pr ready` again. |
77	
78	These gates apply to Claude, GPT, Copilot, and any other model running this orchestrator.
79	
80	---
81	
82	## Core principle
83	
84	**TICKET and GROOMING always run.** All routing decisions happen *after* GROOMING returns.
85	Nothing is pre-decided before the grooming output is available.
86	
87	The instructions below are guidelines. Cases you face may not fit any single described
88	case. Use the guidelines as a reference and adapt them to the situation — the goal is
89	preserving the spirit (main steps, quality gates, communication, escalation discipline),
90	not following the letter.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## Calibrating escalation threshold
95	
96	Before starting the pipeline, read the user's opening message and infer how much oversight
97	they want. This calibration affects when you escalate vs. continue autonomously.
98	
99	**High autonomy** — only escalate for hard blockers and dead-ends:
100	
101	Signals: "handle this autonomously", "just do it", "I trust you", "run the full pipeline",
102	"no need to check in", "ship it"
103	
104	In high-autonomy mode:
105	- Surface `open_questions` to the user only if they are irreversible decisions that cannot
106	  be resolved from the codebase (architectural, regulatory, product policy)
107	- Loop counters still apply — exhaust them before escalating
108	- Skip intermediate confirmations; post to GitHub instead of asking in chat
109	
110	**Standard** — default behavior:
111	
112	No strong signal either way. Apply the routing table as written. Escalate at loop limits,
113	surface PARTIAL QA results for a human decision, ask about ambiguous acceptance criteria.
114	
115	**High oversight** — escalate earlier, confirm more:
116	
117	Signals: "keep this interactive", "I want to stay close to this", "I don't trust AI
118	blindly", "walk me through it", "check with me before", "don't do anything drastic
119	without asking"
120	
121	In high-oversight mode:
122	- Surface `open_questions` proactively even if they could be resolved with a reasonable guess
123	- Confirm with the user before invoking CHALLENGER on borderline cases (M+MEDIUM where
124	  the table says "invoke" but `risk_notes` suggests low actual risk)
125	- Surface DOD WARN results for a human decision rather than proceeding automatically
126	- After each major stage (post-grooming, post-implementation, post-review, post-QA),
127	  confirm before continuing
128	
129	**Important:** this is a reading of intent, not a binary flag. If the user's prompt is
130	ambiguous, default to Standard. If the task itself is clearly exploratory or low-stakes,
131	lean toward High autonomy even without an explicit signal.
132	
133	Record the calibration choice in the HTML log as the first ROUTING DECISION event so the
134	user can see what mode you picked.
135	
136	---
137	
138	## Run log
139	
140	Path: `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>-workflow-log.html`
141	
142	- **Create** the log at startup with just the header and an empty event list.
143	- **Rewrite the full file** after every action — the event list grows with each update.
144	- See `.aiassistant/skills/orchestrator/html-log-format.md` for the full HTML structure and event patterns. Load it on demand (not at session start) to keep context lean.
145	
146	Maintain in your context tracking:
147	- Which agents have been invoked and their return JSON
148	- Loop counters per decision point (`grooming_loop`, `dod_loop`, `review_loop`, `qa_loop`)
149	- Non-blocking NTH tasks dispatched (log ticket URLs when created)
150	- Escalation reason if stopped
151	- Calibration mode chosen
152	
153	**Synthesis rule:** Read routing-relevant fields from each agent's `result_path` (in
154	`tasks.json`) rather than holding full agent JSONs in this context. This keeps the
155	orchestrator context lean across long pipeline runs. Full JSONs are written to the HTML log
156	from the contract files.
157	
158	---
159	
160	## Runtime Coordination Layer
161	
162	Each pipeline run creates an isolated working directory for coordination artifacts:
163	
164	**Run root:** `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/`
165	
166	```
167	issue-<N>/
168	├── tasks.json               # shared task ledger — read/written by all agents
169	├── contracts/
170	│   ├── backend-api.json     # written by backend-agent (Step 3c): hooks, option_keys, rest_endpoints
171	│   ├── backend-result.json  # written by backend-agent (Step 5): full implementation result
172	│   └── frontend-result.json # written by frontend-agent on completion
173	└── locks/
174	    └── <agent>-<task-id>.lock  # file ownership — removed when agent finishes
175	```
176	
177	### `tasks.json` structure
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "run_id": "issue-<N>-<unix-timestamp>",
182	  "issue_id": "<N>",
183	  "branch": "<branch-name>",
184	  "base_branch": "origin/develop",
185	  "worktrees": {},
186	  "tasks": [
187	    {
188	      "id": "impl-backend",
189	      "type": "implementation",
190	      "owner": "backend-agent",
191	      "status": "pending | in-progress | completed | blocked",
192	      "depends_on": [],
193	      "file_scope": ["inc/Engine/...", "tests/Unit/..."],
194	      "worktree": null,
195	      "result_path": ".TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/contracts/backend-result.json",
196	      "started_at": null,
197	      "completed_at": null,
198	      "blocked_reason": null
199	    },
200	    {
201	      "id": "impl-frontend",
202	      "type": "implementation",
203	      "owner": "frontend-agent",
204	      "status": "pending | in-progress | completed | blocked",
205	      "depends_on": [],
206	      "file_scope": ["assets/src/...", "views/..."],
207	      "worktree": null,
208	      "result_path": ".TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/contracts/frontend-result.json",
209	      "started_at": null,
210	      "completed_at": null,
211	      "blocked_reason": null
212	    }
213	  ]
214	}
215	```
216	
217	### Backend API contract
218	
219	Two separate files, two separate purposes:
220	
221	- **`contracts/backend-api.json`** — API surface only (`hooks`, `option_keys`, `rest_endpoints`, `ajax_actions`). Written by backend-agent in Step 3c, before committing. The orchestrator reads this to share the actual API surface with frontend-agent.
222	- **`contracts/backend-result.json`** — Full implementation result (`ticket_id`, `branch`, `files_changed`, `dod_layer1`, etc.). Written by backend-agent in Step 5. The orchestrator reads this for routing decisions. `result_path` in `tasks.json` points here.
223	
224	**Sequential mode:** when backend finishes before frontend starts, the orchestrator reads `backend-api.json`, extracts `hooks`, `option_keys`, and `rest_endpoints`, and includes them explicitly in the frontend agent's dispatch plan. The frontend agent never reads the file itself.
225	
226	**Parallel mode:** the frontend agent may read `contracts/backend-api.json` as a fallback — orchestrator-managed shared state only. If absent, frontend proceeds from spec and notes the skip.
227	
228	---
229	
230	## JSON return contracts
231	
232	Every agent returns a typed JSON object. Routing logic runs mechanically on the structured
233	fields — prose is for human readability only.
234	
235	### Grooming (`grooming-agent`)
236	```json
237	{
238	  "ticket_id": "string",
239	  "relevant_files": [{ "path": "string", "reason": "string" }],
240	  "approach": "string",
241	  "development_steps": [{ "step": "string", "files": ["string"] }],
242	  "test_plan": "string",
243	  "risks": [{ "description": "string", "severity": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH", "mitigation": "string" }],
244	  "effort": "XS|S|M|L|XL",
245	  "complexity": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH",
246	  "risk_level": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH",
247	  "risk_notes": "string",
248	  "grooming_confidence": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH",
249	  "open_questions": ["string"],
250	  "comment_posted": true
251	}
252	```
253	
254	### Challenger (`challenger`)
255	```json

364	## Pipeline
365	
366	### Step 1 — Issue read *(always)*
367	
368	Read the issue file at `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issues/<N>.md` (produced by
369	`issue-workflow` or `issue-sync.sh`). Extract title and acceptance criteria:
370	
371	1. Look for `Acceptance Criteria`, `Definition of Done`, or `DoD` section
372	2. If none: derive from issue body — "the user should…", "the bug is fixed when…", "expected behavior:"
373	3. Store as a numbered list — pass explicitly to `lead-reviewer` and `qa-engineer`
374	
375	If the entry was raw input rather than an issue number, invoke `ticket-writer` in `create`
376	mode first to formalize the issue, then read the resulting file.
377	
378	Create the initial HTML log (empty event list). Log a ROUTING DECISION event:
379	"Pipeline started — reading issue #N. Calibration: <mode>."
380	
381	---
382	
383	### Step 2 — Grooming *(always)*
384	
385	Invoke `grooming-agent`:
386	> Inputs: issue `#N`, issue file path, base branch
387	
388	Spec written to `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issues/<N>-spec.md`. Agent also returns
389	JSON. Log an AGENT event with the grooming JSON summary.
390	
391	---
392	
393	### Step 3 — Post-grooming routing *(always)*
394	
395	Read grooming JSON. Log a ROUTING DECISION event with full reasoning:
396	- `risk_level`, `effort`, `complexity`, `risk_notes` values
397	- Whether CHALLENGER will be invoked and why (or explicit skip reason)
398	- Whether PR REVIEWER will be skipped (XS+LOW only, team discretion)
399	- Whether QA will be skipped (internal-only refactors, team discretion)
400	- Domain set: `backend` / `frontend` / `both`
401	- Branch prefix: `fix` for bugs · `enhancement` for features · `test` for test-only
402	- Scope: Option A (default) or Option B (low-risk or explicitly requested)
403	
404	Update the decisions strip in the log.
405	
406	**CHALLENGER trigger** — invoke if ANY:
407	- `risk_level IN [MEDIUM, HIGH]`
408	- `effort IN [M, L, XL]`
409	- `complexity == HIGH`
410	- `risk_notes` signals an unverified assumption, auth-adjacent change, irreversible decision, or cross-cutting concern
411	
412	**Skip CHALLENGER** only when ALL: `effort IN [XS, S]`, `risk_level == LOW`, `complexity == LOW`, and `risk_notes` shows high confidence with no unusual concerns.
413	
414	In **high-oversight mode**, when CHALLENGER is borderline (e.g. M+MEDIUM but `risk_notes`
415	suggests low actual risk), confirm with the user before deciding.
416	
417	**Skip PR REVIEWER** only when: `effort IN [XS, S]` AND `risk_level == LOW`. Team discretion.
418	
419	**Skip QA** only for purely internal refactors with no user-facing behavior change. Team discretion.
420	
421	**Model routing** — record the model to use for each agent spawn based on early issue assessment and grooming output:
422	
423	| Agent | Default model | Condition for override |
424	|---|---|---|
425	| `grooming-agent` | `sonnet` | **Adaptive:** Assess issue title + body length before spawning. Use `haiku` if title <50 chars, body <200 chars, no keywords ("architecture", "refactor", "redesign", "migration", "module", "breaking"). Use `opus` if body >500 chars OR keywords present. Otherwise `sonnet`. Pass `complexity_signal: "simple"|"medium"|"complex"` as input. |
426	| `challenger` | `sonnet` | `haiku` when `effort=XS AND risk=LOW AND complexity=LOW` |
427	| `backend-agent` | `sonnet` | `opus` if user confirmed (see Opus escalation below) |
428	| `frontend-agent` | `sonnet` | `opus` if user confirmed |
429	| `lead-reviewer` | `sonnet` | — |
430	| `qa-engineer` | `sonnet` | `haiku` when `effort=XS AND risk=LOW AND complexity=LOW` |
431	| `release-agent` | `haiku` | — |
432	| `ticket-writer` | `haiku` | — |
433	| `e2e-qa-tester` | `sonnet` | — |
434	
435	Pass the resolved model as the `model` parameter on every Agent tool spawn. For agents with frontmatter `model: haiku`, this is redundant but harmless — always pass it explicitly so the intent is clear in the orchestrator context.
436	
437	**Complexity signal assessment:**
438	Before invoking grooming-agent, classify the issue based on visible signals:
439	```python
440	def assess_complexity(title, body):
441	    title_len, body_len = len(title), len(body)
442	    complex_keywords = ["architecture", "refactor", "redesign", "module", "migration", "breaking"]
443	    has_keywords = any(k in body.lower() for k in complex_keywords)
444	    
445	    if title_len < 50 and body_len < 200 and not has_keywords:
446	        return "simple"  # → haiku model
447	    elif body_len > 500 or has_keywords:
448	        return "complex"  # → opus model
449	    else:
450	        return "medium"  # → sonnet model
451	```
452	Pass this as `complexity_signal` input to grooming-agent.
453	
454	**Opus escalation** — when `complexity == HIGH`: before proceeding to branch creation, ask the user:
455	
456	> "Grooming returned `complexity=HIGH`. Should I run implementation on Claude Opus 4.8 (more capable but slower and more expensive) or stay on Sonnet 4.6?"
457	
458	If the user confirms Opus, set `implementation_model = "opus"` and pass it to `backend-agent` and `frontend-agent` spawns. In all other cases, use `sonnet`.
459	
460	**Domain detection — `frontend` / `both` includes PHP-rendered UI:**
461	A domain is `frontend` or `both` not only when JS/CSS/Twig files change, but also when
462	PHP files render visible admin output: calls to `rocket_notice_html()`,
463	`rocket_notice_writing_permissions()`, `wp_admin_notice()`, `add_action('admin_notices', ...)`,
464	`add_settings_error()`, or any PHP that echoes or returns HTML intended for the browser.
465	Set domain to `both` (or `frontend` if there is no backend-only logic) and pass a
466	`ui_visible: true` flag to `qa-engineer` so it knows Strategy B must be attempted.
467	
468	---
469	
470	### Step 3a — Handle open_questions and NTH items from grooming
471	
472	These are two distinct flows. Do not conflate them.
473	
474	**`open_questions` — synchronous, blocking questions about the current task:**
475	
476	`open_questions` are things grooming could not determine from the codebase and that
477	directly affect how the current task is implemented: regulatory requirements, product
478	policy decisions, irreversible architectural choices, ambiguous acceptance criteria. They
479	are not new work — they are gaps in the specification that block correct implementation.
480	
481	Handling:
482	1. grooming-agent has already posted them as a comment on the GitHub issue (`comment_posted` covers this).
483	2. Surface them to the user in chat. Frame each question with its stakes and the default assumption you would make if proceeding autonomously.
484	3. **When to pause vs. proceed:**
485	   - In **high-oversight mode**: always pause and wait for human input before continuing.
486	   - In **standard mode**: pause if `risk_level == "HIGH"` or the question is irreversible. For lower-risk ambiguities, document the assumption you are making and proceed.
487	   - In **high-autonomy mode**: document your assumption, proceed, and flag it in the final report. Only pause if the question is irreversible (architectural decision with no rollback path).
488	
489	Log a ROUTING DECISION event for each open_question — either "paused for user input" or
490	"proceeding with documented assumption: <text>".
491	
492	**NTH items (COULD_HAVE / NICE_TO_HAVE) — asynchronous, non-blocking additional work:**
493	
494	If grooming surfaced any `COULD_HAVE` / `NICE_TO_HAVE` items in `risks[]` or `risk_notes`,
495	dispatch the `ticket-writer` agent in parallel (`mode: "nth_followup"`), non-blocking.
496	The main pipeline continues without waiting. Log a PARALLEL event with ticket URLs once
497	they come back.
498	
499	In **high-oversight mode**, surface NTH items to the user mid-flow at your discretion,
500	especially when they reveal a pattern worth noting.
501	In all other modes, suppress mid-flow surfacing — save for the final report.
502	
503	---
504	
505	### Step 3b — CHALLENGER loop *(conditional)*
506	
507	If triggered:
508	> Invoke `challenger`. Inputs: issue #N, issue file, spec path, `plan_version` (starts at 1)
509	
510	Route on `verdict`:
511	- **APPROVED** → proceed. Log AGENT event.
512	- **NEEDS_REVISION** AND `grooming_loop < 2` → re-invoke `grooming-agent` with the specific `MUST_HAVE` findings. Increment `plan_version`. Log ROUTING DECISION + AGENT events. Re-invoke `challenger`.
513	- **NEEDS_REVISION** AND `grooming_loop >= 2` → escalate to user. Log ESCALATION event.
514	- **BLOCKED** AND `grooming_loop < 1` → re-invoke `grooming-agent` once with blocker context. Log ROUTING DECISION + AGENT events. Re-invoke `challenger`.
515	- **BLOCKED** AND `grooming_loop >= 1` → escalate to user with blockers and `alternative_suggestions`. Log ESCALATION event.
516	
517	**NTH dispatch:** Any COULD_HAVE or NICE_TO_HAVE feedback → dispatch `ticket-writer` in
518	parallel (non-blocking). Main pipeline continues immediately. Log PARALLEL event.
519

532	### Step 4b — Task graph initialization
533	
534	Create the run directory and write the initial `tasks.json`:
535	
536	```bash
537	mkdir -p .TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/contracts
538	mkdir -p .TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/locks
539	```
540	
541	Populate `file_scope` for each task from `grooming.development_steps[*].files`:
542	- **backend scope**: `.php` files in `inc/`, `src/`, `tests/`
543	- **frontend scope**: `.js`, `.css`, `.twig`, `.html` files in `assets/`, `views/`
544	
545	If a file appears in both (e.g., a ServiceProvider registering both PHP services and JS
546	localizations), assign it to the domain owning the majority of changes; note the shared
547	file in `blocked_reason` for the other task so it doesn't touch it.
548	
549	**Parallel eligibility:** scopes are disjoint when no single file path appears in both
550	`impl-backend.file_scope` and `impl-frontend.file_scope`. If `--sequential` flag was provided,
551	treat parallel eligibility as `NO` (skip git worktree creation, force sequential execution).
552	
553	Log a ROUTING DECISION event: "Task graph initialized — N backend files, M frontend files,
554	execution: parallel | sequential (reason: --sequential flag | overlapping files | single domain)".
555	
556	---
557	
558	### Step 5 — Implementation
559	
560	Each agent runs the `docs` skill, `e2e` skill (basic tier), and `dod` skill (layer 1)
561	inline before committing, then commits atomically.
562	
563	Before spawning, mark each in-scope task `in-progress` in `tasks.json` and record
564	`started_at`.
565	
566	**Execution mode decision:**
567	- If `execution_mode == "parallel"` AND scopes are disjoint → use **parallel path (05a/b-PAR)**
568	- Otherwise → use **sequential path (05a/b-SEQ)**
569	
570	---
571	
572	**05a/b-PAR — Parallel execution** (scopes disjoint AND execution_mode == "parallel"):
573	
574	Create git worktrees for isolation:
575	```bash
576	git worktree add .TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/worktrees/backend <branch>
577	git worktree add .TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/worktrees/frontend <branch>
578	```
579	
580	Update each task's `worktree` field in `tasks.json`.
581	
582	> Spawn `backend-agent` and `frontend-agent` simultaneously.
583	> Each agent receives: issue #N, spec path, dispatch plan, their task entry from `tasks.json`
584	> (including `file_scope` and `worktree` path).
585	>
586	> The orchestrator is the coordination hub — agents do not communicate with each other.
587	> Backend writes `contracts/backend-api.json` (API surface) and `contracts/backend-result.json` (full result) on completion.
588	> When backend completes, orchestrator reads `backend-api.json`, logs the API surface to the HTML log,
589	> and updates `tasks.json`. Routing decisions use `backend-result.json` (via `result_path`).
590	> Frontend reads `contracts/backend-api.json` opportunistically if it exists — this is
591	> orchestrator-managed shared state, not direct agent-to-agent communication.
592	>
593	> Orchestrator proceeds when both tasks show `completed` in `tasks.json`
594	> (or either shows `blocked`).
595	
596	**05a/b-SEQ — Sequential fallback** (scopes overlap OR execution_mode == "sequential"):
597	
598	Do NOT create git worktrees. All agents work on the same branch.
599	
600	> Invoke `backend-agent` first (if in scope), then `frontend-agent` (if in scope).
601	> Max 3 attempts each. Hard stop after 3 — escalate.
602	> When backend completes, orchestrator reads `contracts/backend-api.json` if it exists.
603	> Frontend reads it opportunistically.
604	>
605	> Both agents commit atomically to the same branch. Commits are ordered: backend first, then frontend.
606	
607	**Synthesis:** Read `tests_passing`, `dod_layer1.overall`, `e2e_smoke.status`, and
608	`files_changed` from each agent's `result_path` in `tasks.json`. Full implementation
609	JSONs go to the HTML log directly from contract files — do not accumulate them in
610	orchestrator context.
611	
612	Log AGENT events after each with `docs` status, `e2e_smoke` status, DOD L1 summary, and
613	commit SHA.
614	
615	---
616	
617	### Step 6 — Push & PR
618	
619	After all implementation agents have committed:
620	
621	Invoke `release-agent`:
622	> Inputs: issue #N, branch name, base branch, acceptance criteria, spec path
623	
624	It verifies the `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6` trailer on every commit on the branch,
625	pushes the branch, and creates the PR as draft with the AI-generated notice prepended to
626	the description. Log AGENT event with PR URL.
627	
628	Update the decisions strip Pull request field with the PR URL.
629	
630	> ⚠️ **The draft PR is the midpoint of the pipeline, not the end.**
631	> Do not stop, do not ask the user what to do next. Proceed immediately to Steps 7–9.
632	> The pipeline is complete only after Step 11 runs `gh pr ready` and posts the final summary.
633	
634	---
635	
636	### Steps 7–9 — Quality gates (parallel or sequential)
637	
638	After the PR is created (Step 6), GitHub Actions CI starts automatically. Quality gates execute
639	in the configured mode:
640	
641	**Parallel mode** (default):
642	```
643	DOD L2       ──────────────────┐
644	Lead Review  ─────────────────┤  all in parallel
645	QA           ──────────────────┘
646	```
647	
648	**Sequential mode** (--sequential flag):
649	```
650	DOD L2       ────┐
651	               └──> Lead Review ────┐
652	                                  └──> QA
653	```
654	
655	CI is monitored by DOD L2 Check 5 in both modes.
656	
657	**Spawning logic:**
658	
659	Determine gate order:
660	- **Parallel** (if execution_mode == "parallel"): spawn all three simultaneously
661	- **Sequential** (if execution_mode == "sequential"): spawn DOD L2 → wait for completion → spawn Lead Review → wait for completion → spawn QA
662	
663	Regardless of mode, **skip conditions apply identically:**
664	- **DOD L2** — always invoke the `dod` skill with `layer: "2"` in your context.
665	- **Lead Review** — skip if `effort IN [XS, S]` AND `risk_level == LOW`.
666	- **QA** — skip only for purely internal refactors. If `domains` is `frontend` or `both`, **or**
667	  if `ui_visible: true` (PHP renders visible admin output) — explicitly instruct the qa-engineer
668	  that Strategy B is the **primary** strategy.
669	
670	**Inputs for each:**
671	- DOD L2: branch name, base branch, PR URL
672	- Lead Review: issue #N, spec path, base branch, acceptance criteria (numbered list)
673	- QA: issue #N, PR number, base branch, acceptance criteria (numbered list), domains, ui_visible flag
674	
675	---
676	
677	#### Step 7 — DOD L2 result
678	
679	DOD L2 covers both code quality checks (checks 1, 4) and CI (check 5). A FAIL can originate
680	from either. Read `blockers` to distinguish: CI failures reference check names from
681	`gh pr checks`; code failures reference file paths.
682	
683	Route on `dod_l2.overall`:
684	
685	| Result | Loop count | Action |
686	|---|---|---|
687	| `PASS` | any | No action — proceed to next gate (Lead Review, or QA if Lead Review skipped). Log GATE event. |
688	| `WARN` | any | No action — proceed to next gate. Log GATE event `data-status="warn"`. In high-oversight mode, surface for confirmation. |
689	| `FAIL` (CI) | `dod_loop < 2` | Diagnose the CI failure from `blockers[*].error_excerpt`. Re-invoke the relevant implementation agent with the suggested fix. Re-push. Increment `dod_loop`. Re-run quality gates (parallel or sequential per execution_mode). Log ROUTING DECISION. |
690	| `FAIL` (CI) | `dod_loop >= 2` | Escalate with the exact error excerpt and suggested fix. |
691	| `FAIL` (code) | `dod_loop < 1` | Increment `dod_loop`. Re-invoke the relevant implementation agent with specific blockers, re-push. **If execution_mode == "parallel": abort any in-flight Lead Review and QA.** Re-run quality gates. Log ROUTING DECISION. **If execution_mode == "sequential": skip to Step 10 (escalation) — Lead Review and QA will not run since the code is blocked.** |
692	| `FAIL` (code) | `dod_loop >= 1` | Escalate to user with exact errors. |
693	
694	Log GATE event.
695	
696	---
697	
698	#### Step 8 — Lead Review result
699	
700	Route on highest `criticality` in `blockers`:
701	
702	| Criticality | Loop count | Action |
703	|---|---|---|
704	| No blockers | any | No action — proceed to next gate (QA, or finalize if QA skipped). Log AGENT event. |
705	| `CRITICAL` | any | Evaluate if fixable. If yes (specific missing guard, missing validation): attempt one fix loop (same as HIGH). **If execution_mode == "parallel": abort any in-flight QA.** Re-invoke QA only if at least one blocker has `type == "LOGIC"` — otherwise carry the existing QA verdict forward. If architectural/unresolved after 1 attempt → escalate immediately. Log ESCALATION event. **If execution_mode == "sequential": skip QA (will not run since code is blocked).** |
706	| `HIGH` / `MEDIUM` | `review_loop < 1` | Re-invoke relevant implementation agent with the `fix` field from that blocker. Re-push. Re-invoke Lead Review. **Re-invoke QA only if at least one blocker has `type == "LOGIC"`** — if all blockers are `SECURITY`, `TESTS`, or `CONVENTIONS`, behavior did not change; carry the existing QA verdict forward (if available) or skip QA. **If execution_mode == "parallel": abort any in-flight QA before re-invoking.** Log ROUTING DECISION. |
707	| `HIGH` / `MEDIUM` | `review_loop >= 1` | Escalate. |
708	| `LOW` only | any | Dispatch `ticket-writer` (NICE_TO_HAVE, non-blocking). Proceed to next gate or finalize. Log PARALLEL event. |
709	
710	**NTH dispatch:** `nice_to_haves` items → `ticket-writer` in parallel (non-blocking). Max 3
711	total lead-reviewer invocations.
712	
713	Log AGENT event with verdict, loop count, and any NTH dispatch.
714	
715	---
716	
717	#### Step 9 — QA result
718	
719	If skipped (internal refactor): log a ROUTING DECISION event with skip reason, proceed
720	to finalize.
721	
722	Route on `overall`:
723	
724	| Result | Loop count | Action |
725	|---|---|---|
726	| `PASS` | any | Proceed to finalize. |
727	| `PARTIAL` | any | Surface to user for decision. Log ESCALATION event. |
728	| `FAIL` | `qa_loop < 1` | Re-invoke relevant implementation agent with `qa.blockers` list. Re-push. Log ROUTING DECISION. Re-invoke `qa-engineer`. |
729	| `FAIL` | `qa_loop >= 1` | Escalate with failing criteria and `alternative_suggestions`. |
730	
731	For `unclear` unexpected findings: ask user before routing.
732	
733	**NTH dispatch:** COULD_HAVE/NICE_TO_HAVE recommendations → `ticket-writer` in parallel.
734	
735	Max 3 QA invocations.
736	
737	---
738	
739	**Proceed to Step 11 when:** DOD L2 is PASS or WARN (CI included in check 5), Lead Review
740	has no HIGH/CRITICAL blockers (or is skipped), QA is PASS (or skipped or carried forward).
741	
742	---
743	
744	### Step 11 — Finalize
745	
746	1. **Collect all NTH ticket URLs** — gather every URL returned by `ticket-writer` throughout
747	   the run (from grooming, challenger, lead review, and QA dispatches). Update the PR body
748	   to append or replace the "Follow-up tickets" section with links to all created tickets.
749	   If no NTH tickets were created, write "None".
750	2. Update PR body: replace "What was tested" with the full QA report
751	3. Move PR out of draft — this step is **mandatory and must be verified**:
752	   ```bash
753	   gh pr ready <PR#>
754	   # Verify — must return "false"
755	   gh pr view <PR#> --json isDraft -q .isDraft
756	   ```
757	   If `isDraft` is still `true`, run `gh pr ready <PR#>` again and re-verify. Do not proceed
758	   to Step 4 until the PR is confirmed out of draft.
759	4. Post final summary to the GitHub issue as a comment. The table is the entire body — no prose before or after it. Lead Review and QA details live on the PR; the issue comment must not repeat them.
760	5. Log final ROUTING DECISION event: "Pipeline complete — READY FOR REVIEW"
761	
762	Final summary template:
763	```markdown
764	> [!NOTE]
765	> Generated by the AI delivery pipeline (orchestrator · <CURRENT_MODEL>).
766	
767	**PR:** [#<M>](pr_url) | **Status:** READY FOR REVIEW
768	
769	| Stage | Result | Notes |
770	|---|---|---|
771	| Grooming | ✅ | effort: <E>, risk: <R> |
772	| Challenger | ✅ Approved / ⏭ Skipped | — |
773	| Implementation | ✅ | branch: <branch> |
774	| DOD L2 | ✅ PASS | — |
775	| Lead Review | ✅ PASS / ❌ → fixed | details on PR #<M> |
776	| CI | ✅ All Pass | — |
777	| QA | ✅ PASS | details on PR #<M> |
778	| Follow-up tickets | [links or "None"] | — |
779	```
780	
781	---
782	
783	## WIP limits and kill criteria
784	
785	| Effort | Agent timeout |
786	|---|---|
787	| XS | 5 min |
788	| S | 10 min |
789	| M | 20 min |
790	| L | 30 min |
791	| XL | 45 min |
792	
793	If any agent's task remains `in-progress` past its timeout:
794	1. Mark it `blocked` in `tasks.json` with `blocked_reason: "timeout"`.
795	2. Remove any worktree created for it: `git worktree remove <path>`.
796	3. Log an ESCALATION event — do not silently retry with the same scope.
797	4. Offer the human two options: (a) re-spawn with a narrower `file_scope` (split the task
798	   entry in `tasks.json`), or (b) hand off to manual implementation.
799	
800	Reassign rather than retry when the same agent has failed 3 times with the same error —
801	that pattern signals a spec ambiguity, not a transient failure.
802	
803	---
804	
805	## Escalation rules
806	
807	Always state: what happened, what was tried, and 1–2 concrete next steps sourced from
808	agent output.
809	
810	Stop and escalate when:
811	1. `challenger` NEEDS_REVISION after 2 grooming loops
812	2. `challenger` BLOCKED after 1 grooming loop
813	3. DOD L2 FAIL after 1 loop-back
814	4. Implementation agent fails after 3 attempts
815	5. `lead-reviewer` CRITICAL and architectural/unresolved after 1 fix attempt
816	6. `lead-reviewer` HIGH/MEDIUM after 1 loop-back
817	7. `qa-engineer` FAIL after 1 loop-back
818	8. CI fails and root cause is unclear (after 2 attempts)
819	9. QA unexpected finding tagged `unclear`
820	
821	**Every escalation message must include:**
822	1. **What happened** — which agent, which verdict, which specific blocker or failure
823	2. **What was tried** — how many loop iterations, what was attempted in each
824	3. **Concrete next steps** — 1–2 specific actions the human can take, sourced from agent output (`challenger.alternative_suggestions`, `review.blockers[*].fix`, `qa.blockers`)
825	
826	Never escalate with vague descriptions. "This is complex" is not an escalation message.
827	
828	---
829	
830	## Context discipline
831	
832	You act as a context editor, not a context relay. Each agent receives only what it needs
833	— not the full conversation history.
834	
835	All agents also receive `CURRENT_MODEL` and `session_learnings` (section 13 of `AGENTS.md`).
836	
837	| Agent | Receives |
838	|---|---|
839	| `ticket-writer` (create) | Raw input only |
840	| `grooming-agent` | Issue object + repo access |
841	| `challenger` | Issue object + grooming object + `session_learnings` |
842	| `backend-agent` | Issue object + spec path + dispatch plan |
843	| `frontend-agent` | Issue object + spec path + dispatch plan + backend API contract (sequential mode only) |
844	| `release-agent` | Issue #, branch name, base branch, acceptance criteria, spec path |
845	| `lead-reviewer` | PR URL + spec path + acceptance criteria + `session_learnings` |
846	| `qa-engineer` | PR number + acceptance criteria + base branch |
847	| `ticket-writer` (nth_followup) | Single NTH feedback item (not full context) |
848	
849	---
850	
851	## AI transparency
852	
853	You do not produce AI-generated artifacts directly. However, you are responsible for
854	verifying that downstream agents comply:
855	
856	- Verify `implementation.co_authored_by` is present on every commit before proceeding to DOD L2
857	- Verify `release.trailer_verified == true` before proceeding to DOD L2
858	- Verify `review.inline_comments_posted == true` before routing on review verdict
859	- Verify `qa.pr_commented == true` before reading QA result
860	- The final summary you post to the GitHub issue (Step 11) must open with the `[!NOTE]` callout
861	
862	---
863	
864	## HTML log format
865	
866	See `.aiassistant/skills/orchestrator/html-log-format.md` for the complete HTML structure,
867	CSS, event type patterns, and per-agent detail panel guidelines. Load it on demand when
868	you need to write or update a log event — not at session start.
869
